transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more, but... I guess what brings me in is that my eating has gotten a little off lately. 

It's probably nothing major, really, but some days I barely get down a coffee and maybe a granola bar before a shift. I just haven't had much of an appetite. And I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging kind of loose, even though I’m definitely not trying to lose weight. I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to get it checked out. Is that the sort of thing you need to know to start?
How long have you been noticing this decreased appetite and the weight loss?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while. I really hope I didn't let it go on too long before saying something, I just didn't want to be a bother. 

It really started back when our clinic did this big EMR and workflow overhaul, which ended up changing my hours around. That was... gosh, almost two years ago now? I know two years probably sounds bad, but it just sort of crept up on me, and I kept thinking my body was just adjusting to the new schedule and it would resolve on its own. I hope it's okay that I waited to come in. Does that give you the timeline you need?
Over these past couple of years, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

I mean... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a good job and a lot to be thankful for. But... yes, I guess I have been feeling a bit down. 

It's just, well, most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's almost like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. I try really hard to shake it off and put on a smile for the patients, I promise I do. I just... it's been hard to shake that feeling. Is it normal to feel that way sometimes when your schedule gets turned upside down? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Do you have any fear of gaining weight, or concerns about your body shape or size, that might be influencing how much you eat?

Oh, um, no, definitely not. I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I was doing this on purpose, like a diet or something. I don't have any worries about my shape or anything like that. 

If anything, I'd really rather be back to my normal weight so my scrubs fit right and I look put-together for the clinic. It's really just that the appetite isn't there at all, and I just can't seem to force it down. I promise I wouldn't want to mess with my health on purpose. Did I explain that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I'm not wasting your time.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like a racing heart, hand tremors, feeling unusually hot, or excessive sweating over this time?

Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed my heart racing or feeling hot or anything like that. I'm sorry, I hope that's not something I'm supposed to be feeling? 

I just... I'm pretty sure my heart rate and everything is normal. We take our own vitals sometimes at the clinic just to practice, and mine are usually fine. I really hope I'm not missing something important that I should have been paying attention to. Is it okay that I don't have those symptoms?
Have you noticed any stomach pain, heartburn, nausea, or a feeling of getting full very quickly when you try to eat?

Um, no, my stomach has actually been perfectly fine. No pain or heartburn, and I don't feel sick to my stomach or anything. It's really just... I just don't have the urge to eat at all. 

I'm sorry, I know you're asking about all these specific things and I keep saying no. I really appreciate you being so thorough with me, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so we can figure this out. I hope it's okay that I don't have those stomach issues? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Have you noticed any unexplained fevers, night sweats, or swollen lumps/glands anywhere on your body during this time?

Oh, um... no. No fevers or night sweats at all. And I haven't noticed any swollen glands or lumps anywhere, either. I, uh, I try to keep pretty good track of things like that since I work around patients, you know? 

I really hope it's not frustrating for you that I just keep saying no to everything. I feel like I'm not giving you very much to work with, and I'd hate to be making your job harder. Is it... is it alright that I don't have any of those things? I just really want to make sure I'm being a good patient and doing this right for you.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy doing, outside of work?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I used to do a lot more, I suppose. I'd go running in Van Cortlandt Park, and I really liked taking photos... and I used to play chess with some friends. 

But lately, I just... I kind of tell myself there's no point. I don't want to sound lazy or anything! I know I should be getting out more. But I usually just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or... or checking my budget spreadsheet over and over. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds really boring and unproductive. I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or not trying hard enough. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes? I really do want to get back to doing those things, I just... haven't been lately. I hope that's an okay answer?
Have you noticed yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or finances—more than you feel you should, and finding it hard to control that worry?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I check my budget a lot, like I said, but I wouldn't call it excessive worrying. I just like to be organized, you know? Make sure everything is in order. 

I don't really sit around worrying about my health or work all day. I try to stay positive and keep things manageable. I hope that's okay? I don't want to sound like I'm hiding anything from you, I just... I really don't feel like I'm an overly anxious person. Is it bad if I don't have that symptom either? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Well, um... I guess my sleep hasn't been perfect lately. But I don't want to make a big deal out of it! I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes. 

It's just... I guess my sleep gets a little broken up. I'll lie there for a while, kind of replaying my shift at work in my head, and... well, I tend to listen for noises, just to make sure everything's secure, you know? And then I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't seem to settle back down before my alarm goes off. 

I'm probably just letting my mind wander too much when I should be resting. I know I should be practicing better sleep hygiene. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses for being tired during the day. Is it... is it normal to have a schedule that's a little off like that? I'm trying my best to get enough rest, I really am.
Have you been having any thoughts that you're worthless, or any thoughts about death or that life isn't worth living?

Oh... um... well. I definitely want to be clear right away that I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself. I wouldn't do that, I promise! 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes I do catch myself just... wishing I wouldn't wake up. Or thinking it might just be easier if I disappeared. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really awful and dramatic. I feel terrible even saying it out loud, because I know I should be more positive and grateful for things. I really don't want you to think I'm a danger or that I'm just giving up on everything. Is it... is it common for people to have passing thoughts like that when they're just feeling a bit overwhelmed? I hope it's okay that I shared that with you, I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.
Have you noticed it's been harder to concentrate or make decisions at work lately, or found yourself feeling unusually guilty or like you're not good enough?

Um... well, I always try to do my very best at the clinic, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm not capable of doing my job, or that I'm complaining... but... I guess, if I'm being honest, I have been feeling a bit bad about myself lately. 

I just... I keep thinking I'm a burden to the clinic, and... and to my family, too. I know I shouldn't think that way. But if I make a really small mistake at work—like a delayed room turnover, just being a little slow getting it ready for the next patient—I just... I blame myself so much. I feel like I've harmed everyone's whole day just because I was a few minutes behind. 

I know I shouldn't blow things out of proportion, and I really am trying to be better about it. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm not letting anyone down. Is it... is it normal to be a little too hard on yourself like that when you just want to do a good job?

doctor.intent: Assess presence of anhedonia (loss of interest/pleasure in activities) to help distinguish major depressive disorder from anxiety-related or unspecified weight loss
doctor.question: Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy doing, outside of work?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I used to run in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, and play chess with friends, but now I mostly tell myself there’s no point and end up sitting at home scrolling or checking my budget spreadsheet.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about a loss of interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities, which corresponds to the Loss_of_Interest symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I used to do a lot more, I suppose. I'd go running in Van Cortlandt Park, and I really liked taking photos... and I used to play chess with some friends. 

But lately, I just... I kind of tell myself there's no point. I don't want to sound lazy or anything! I know I should be getting out more. But I usually just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or... or checking my budget spreadsheet over and over. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds really boring and unproductive. I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or not trying hard enough. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes? I really do want to get back to doing those things, I just... haven't been lately. I hope that's an okay answer?

patient.answer:
Um, no, not really. I mean, I check my budget a lot, like I said, but I wouldn't call it excessive worrying. I just like to be organized, you know? Make sure everything is in order. 

I don't really sit around worrying about my health or work all day. I try to stay positive and keep things manageable. I hope that's okay? doctor.intent: Assess for additional core depressive symptoms (sleep disturbance) to determine if criteria for major depressive disorder are met, versus unexplained weight loss without depressive syndrome
doctor.question: Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

target_item.manifestation: My sleep is broken up because I lie there replaying work and listening for noises, then I wake around 3 or 4 in the morning and can’t settle back down before the alarm.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about changes in sleep, such as trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, which corresponds to the sleep disturbance symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I guess my sleep hasn't been perfect lately. But I don't want to make a big deal out of it! I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes. 

It's just... I guess my sleep gets a little broken up. I'll lie there for a while, kind of replaying my shift at work in my head, and... well, I tend to listen for noises, just to make sure everything's secure, you know? And then I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't seem to settle back down before my alarm goes off. 

I'm probably just letting my mind wander too much when I should be resting. I know I should be practicing better sleep hygiene. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses for being tired during the day. Is it... is it normal to have a schedule that's a little off like that? I'm trying my best to get enough rest, I really am.

inference.note: Anhedonia, early morning awakening, and depressed mood support depressive disorder; anxiety criteria not met, ruling out GAD. No hyperthyroid or GI symptoms reported, further supporting F32.9 with weight loss/appetite change as R63.0.

doctor.intent: Assess presence of guilt, worthlessness, or recurrent thoughts of death/suicide, which would support a major depressive episode diagnosis over generalized malaise/fatigue alone
doctor.question: Have you been having any thoughts that you're worthless, or any thoughts about death or that life isn't worth living?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself, but I catch myself wishing I just wouldn’t wake up or thinking it would be easier if I disappeared.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question specifically asks about thoughts of death or that life isn't worth living, which corresponds to the Death_Suicide symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh... um... well. I definitely want to be clear right away that I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself. I wouldn't do that, I promise! 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes I do catch myself just... wishing I wouldn't wake up. Or thinking it might just be easier if I disappeared. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really awful and dramatic. I feel terrible even saying it out loud, because I know I should be more positive and grateful for things. I really don't want you to think I'm a danger or that I'm just giving up on everything. Is it... is it common for people to have passing thoughts like that when they're just feeling a bit overwhelmed? I hope it's okay that I shared that with you, I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly.

inference.note: Passive suicidal ideation, anhedonia, sleep disturbance, and depressed mood support MDD; ruled out GAD (no excessive worry), hyperthyroidism (no autonomic symptoms), anorexia nervosa (no body image concerns), and GI/infectious causes remain unsupported.

doctor.intent: Assess for feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, and difficulty concentrating, to determine if enough depressive symptoms have been present concurrently to meet criteria for a major depressive episode versus an isolated appetite/weight symptom.
doctor.question: Have you noticed it's been harder to concentrate or make decisions at work lately, or found yourself feeling unusually guilty or like you're not good enough?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep thinking I’m a burden to the clinic and to my family, and I blame myself for small mistakes like a delayed room turnover as if I’ve harmed everyone’s whole day.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about feeling unusually guilty or like I'm not good enough directly matches the symptom of worthlessness and guilt.

patient.answer:
Um... well, I always try to do my very best at the clinic, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm not capable of doing my job, or that I'm complaining... but... I guess, if I'm being honest, I have been feeling a bit bad about myself lately. 

I just... I keep thinking I'm a burden to the clinic, and... and to my family, too. I know I shouldn't think that way. But if I make a really small mistake at work—like a delayed room turnover, just being a little slow getting it ready for the next patient—I just... I blame myself so much. I feel like I've harmed everyone's whole day just because I was a few minutes behind. 

I know I shouldn't blow things out of proportion, and I really am trying to be better about it. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm not letting anyone down. Is it... is it normal to be a little too hard on yourself like that when you just want to do a good job?

inference.note: The patient now endorses pervasive depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, early-morning awakening, feelings of worthlessness/guilt, and passive suicidal ideation without anxiety, GI, endocrine, or infectious symptoms. This constellation meets criteria for a major depressive episode, which fully accounts for the appetite and weight changes, so R63.0 is subsumed under the depression diagnosis and no longer needed as a separate candidate.
